text:
Kevin (Support): heads-up: AcmePay escalated—large p95/p99 spike after this morning's runtime rollout. They pasted a few request ids: req=rc_a7c1, rc_a7d8, rc_a804. Users report chat completions slowed and occasional gateway 504s.

Anya (SRE): which pool did the canary land on? region? instance-type?

Tim (Runtime): Canary rolled to us-west-2 gpu-nv4-small at 08:52 UTC via deploy-bot. It was 10% traffic. Pulling traces now.

deploy-bot: deploy v2.14 -> canary (10%) started by tim at 2026-03-15T08:52:10Z

Kevin (Support): Observed numbers: p95 from ~430ms -> ~2.6s, p99 to ~6.5s. Spike starts ~15-20m after canary. Errors: mostly 200s with long latency, plus gateway 504s. Endpoints hit: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/generate. Embeddings OK.

Anya (SRE): Any payload shape pattern? long sequences? concurrency?

Kevin (Support): Customer sample: prompt ~620 tokens, response target 512, client concurrency ~5-8.

Tim (Runtime): That matches a heuristic change in v2.14: 1) adaptive batcher rewrite, 2) new fused-attn kernel selector for seq>=512. Both in canary. Early flamegraphs show attention matmul kernel queuing spikes and longer GPU kernel wait times on affected nodes.

perf-bot: telemetry snapshot: pre-canary (08:40-08:50) p95=440ms p99=900ms. Post-canary (09:10-09:30) p95=2.6s p99=6.5s. Error delta +1.9% (gateway timeouts).

Linda (Product): AcmePay is on dedicated capacity but had overflow into shared pool where canary landed briefly. They need stability—escalated to SEs.

Anya (SRE): Immediate actions: (A) rollback canary on the affected nodepool, (B) pin heavy-seq customers to stable runtime, (C) bisect batcher vs kernel changes. Kevin: can you request concrete request bodies for repro?

Kevin (Support): asked AcmePay for example requests and recent logs. They confirmed shapes above.

Tim (Runtime): Initiating rollback for gpu-nv4-small now.

deploy-bot: rollback v2.13 -> gpu-nv4-small started by tim at 2026-03-15T09:18:43Z

Kevin (Support): Customers still see slowness for ~3m after rollback—likely draining in-flight work.

perf-bot: post-rollback (09:22-09:40) p95=500ms p99=1.1s. Error rate back to baseline. Dashboard: https://perf.internal/reports/1898765432

Anya (SRE): Good. Tim: can you create two isolated canaries—one with only the kernel selector change, one with only the batcher rewrite—and run synthetic load that mirrors AcmePay (seq=600, resp_target=512, conc=8)?

Tim (Runtime): On it. Will spin up canary-kernel and canary-batcher pools and run a 10m synthetic workload. Also adding tracing on both GPU and request sides. ETA ~35m.

Linda (Product): Meanwhile, add a temporary routing rule to prefer v2.13 for requests where estimated_sequence_length >= 512. That should protect heavy customers.

Tim (Runtime): I can add a control-plane routing predicate. Example rule snippet I pushed to staging:

```
when request.headers["x-estimated-seq"] >= 512 -> route runtime:v2.13
```

No infra deploy required. Pushing live now.

Kevin (Support): Sending AcmePay a short summary: rollback done, routing rule applied, engineers bisecting cause. They asked for ETA.

Tim (Runtime): Synthetic run results (first pass): kernel-only canary p95=560ms p99=1.5s; batcher-only canary p95=2.0s p99=5.9s; baseline v2.13 p95=460ms p99=980ms.

Anya (SRE): Signals point to batcher rewrite as main contributor. Tim: what do batch-size histograms show?

Tim (Runtime): v2.14 batcher occasionally emits large batches (~64) for seq>=512; previous batcher capped ~32 for that workload. Those oversized batches increase per-request tail when concurrency shapes vary.

Anya (SRE): Proposed mitigation: introduce a soft cap for adaptive batcher for long sequences (max_batch_size=32). Patch in canary-batcher and re-run.

Tim (Runtime): Pushing patch now as env override flag and deploying to canary-batcher-2.

deploy-bot: deploy v2.14-batcher-cap -> canary-batcher-2 started by tim at 2026-03-15T10:17:05Z

perf-bot: canary-batcher-2 10m window: p95=490ms p99=1.15s. Batch-size distribution capped; kernel wait times normalized.

Anya (SRE): That looks promising. Next: promote the batcher cap patch to production pools, remove temporary customer pins once rollout is stable, and plan a permanent fix for adaptive batcher logic. Also add CI perf tests that include long-sequence synthetic workloads.

Tim (Runtime): Opening PR with cap and tests: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4602. Tests simulate seq>=512 shapes and validate batch-size distribution.

Linda (Product): Kevin, please update AcmePay: rollback complete, routing rule active, root cause under investigation is adaptive batcher allowing oversized batches on long sequences; patch applied to production; monitoring/alerts on tail latencies increased retention. Provide a conservative ETA: preliminary RCA in ~3-4 hours, full postmortem in 24-48h.

Kevin (Support): Sent message to customer with that wording; they acknowledged and appreciate the quick mitigation.

Anya (SRE): Follow-ups: add runbook section "Runtime rollout p95/p99 spike checklist" including checks for batch sizes, kernel-selector heuristics, and routing rules. Assign owners: Tim (fix + PR), Anya (validation + runbook), Kevin (customer comms).

Tim (Runtime): I'll monitor for 24h and then remove the temporary routing predicate after confidence window. Marking rollback flag cleared at 11:30 UTC.

deploy-bot: rollback flag cleared by tim at 2026-03-15T11:30:02Z

Anya (SRE): Closing notes: root cause (primary) = adaptive batcher allowed excessively large batches for seq>=512; secondary risk = kernel-selector heuristic shift. Mitigations = batcher max cap, routing rule, additional perf tests. Postmortem owner: Tim.

Kevin (Support): I'll file the PM summary and link Tim's PR and the synthetic run artifacts. Closing escalation unless tail spikes recur in next 24h. Thanks all.
